map.Dungeon level unlocked. Why is the floor: Next level. Why is the floor… smoking?
That is inequality fog. It seals the way out. Just TRUE statements clear it. False ones feed it.
map.The antechamber. Brass balance scales li: The front room. Brass balance scales line the walls. Fog slides over the stairs at the back. The way back is gone.
map.Every scale in here is an equation — a s: Each scale in here is an equation. It says two sides are equal. The stand wants a key.
map.So we test keys the way I test bolts. On: We test keys the way I test bolts. One at a time. We never guess twice.
map.Practice plate: n + 2 = 6. Only n = 4 ke: Test plate: n + 2 = 6. Just n = 4 keeps it true. 4 + 2 really is 6.
map.Correct. A solution is the value that ma: Yes. A solution is the value that makes it TRUE. A wrong key is a lie. The fog likes lies.
map.An equation says two things are equal. A: An equation says two things are equal. A solution is the value that makes it true. Substitute, then check.
map.Reader — you're our fifth crew member. T: Reader, you are on our crew too! Test the keys. TRUE statements only.
map.The pedestal plate reads x + 7 = 15. Fou: The plate on the stand says x + 7 = 15. Four brass keys say 8, 22, 7, 105. The key that makes the plate TRUE will turn. Then the fog asks one more thing. Does y = 6 make 3y = 21 true?
map.Conceptual: a solution is the value that: Conceptual: a solution is a value. It makes an equation TRUE. Substitute the key for x. Then check. Are both sides really equal?
map.Procedural: take a key, add 7 to it, and: Procedural: take a key. Add 7 to it. Do you land right on 15? For the fog's check, find 3 × 6 first. Then answer.
map.The bridge across IS the beam of one gia: The bridge IS the beam of one big scale. It locks level just when both pans match.
map.Left pan: a sealed crate — call its weig: Left pan: a crate plus nine brass weights. Call the crate's weight x. Right pan: fourteen.
map.Practice beam: n + 3 = 10. Lift 3 off BO: Test beam: n + 3 = 10. Take 3 off BOTH pans… n = 7. It never shook.
That undo move is an inverse operation. Subtraction undoes addition. Do it to BOTH sides.
map.Inverse operations undo each other: + an: Inverse operations undo each other: + and −, × and ÷. Balance rule: same move, both sides, each time.
map.Counterweights ready. Reader — level the: Weights are set. Reader, make the beam level so we can cross!
map.The beam locks only when both pans match: The beam locks just when both pans match. Left pan: the crate x plus 9 brass weights. Right pan: 14 weights. Solve x + 9 = 14. Type x. Watch the beam.
map.Conceptual: a scale stays level only if: Conceptual: do the SAME thing to both sides. Then a scale stays level. You want x alone. So the 9 next to it must go. Take it from BOTH pans.
map.Procedural: undo + 9 with its inverse: s: Procedural: undo + 9 with its inverse. Subtract 9 from both sides. x = 14 − 9. Work it out with care.
